title.value: Improving Adversarial Transferability via Model Alignment
title.justification: The title is taken directly from the document provided.
title.quote: Improving Adversarial Transferability via Model Alignment

analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel model alignment technique to improve the transferability of adversarial perturbations generated by neural networks. The technique aligns the parameters of a source model with those of an independently trained witness model by minimizing an alignment loss, thereby enhancing transferability. The effects of this method are demonstrated through geometric analysis of the loss landscape and extensive experiments on the ImageNet dataset.

type.justification: The study conducts extensive experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model alignment technique, which characterizes it as empirical research.
type.quote: Extensive experiments on the ImageNet dataset, using a variety of model architectures, demonstrate that perturbations generated from aligned source models exhibit significantly higher transferability than those from the original source model.

name.justification: The paper focuses on improving the transferability of adversarial perturbations through model alignment, which falls under the domain of adversarial machine learning.
name.quote: Neural networks are susceptible to adversarial perturbations that are transferable across different models. In this paper, we introduce a novel model alignment technique aimed at improving a given source model’s ability in generating transferable adversarial perturbations.

name.justification: The paper deals with the transferability of adversarial examples across different model architectures, which is a key aspect of transfer learning.
name.quote: It has been observed that perturbations created to attack one model can also fool other models, which is known as adversarial transferability.

name.justification: ImageNet, a well-known dataset in computer vision, is used for the experiments, illustrating the paper's relevance to this field.
name.quote: Extensive experiments on the ImageNet dataset, using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) [15,37], demonstrate that perturbations generated from aligned source models exhibit significantly higher transferability.

name.justification: ResNet50 is mentioned as one of the source models used in experiments for model alignment.
name.quote: For CNNs, we include ResNet18 (Res18), ResNet50 (Res50), ResNet101 (Res101) [23], VGG19 [57], DenseNet121 (DN121) [26], and Inception-v3 (IncV3) [59].

is_compared.quote: We compare the transferability of perturbations generated using the source model before and after performing model alignment.
